questions.question:
**Directions: Given below are four jumbled sentences. Select the option that gives their correct order.**

A. In India, forests are huge catchment areas for rivers and streams as they help in storing water.

B. If these forests continue to be felled indiscriminately, rivers and streams will dry up leading to drought.

C. Due to this, many states are facing a shortage of water in the summer months.

D. Unfortunately, these dense forest areas are disappearing.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"ADCB"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence 'A' is independent of any other sentences as it is giving general information about the "forests of India". Hence, 'A' is the first sentence.
 
• Sentence **'D' **gives us more information about the forests mentioned in **'A'**. Hence, 'D' follows 'A'.
 
• The pronoun **'this' **in the phrase "due to this" mentioned in the sentence 'C' refers back to the word "disappearing" mentioned in the sentence 'D'. Hence, 'C' follows 'D'.
 
• The final result of the "cutting down of the forests" is shown in the sentence 'B' and is concluding the paragraph. Hence, 'B' makes the last sentence.​__

 

__Paragraph after rearranging the sentences__: *In India, forests are huge catchment areas for rivers and streams as they help in storing water. Unfortunately, these dense forest areas are disappearing. Due to this, many states are facing a shortage of water in the summer months. If these forests continue to be felled indiscriminately, rivers and streams will dry up leading to drought*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• Important Rules to Solve the Para Jumbles__:

 
 
• Read the sentences attentively and try to comprehend the idea or theme of the paragraph.
 
• Try to identify the opening and closing sentences of the paragraph. Try to identify the mandatory pairs.
 
• Sometimes it is not necessary to identify all the sentences, we can arrange the sentences by eliminating the irrelevant option one by one.

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the correct passive form of the given sentence.**

I use jaggery to sweeten my tea in winters.

options.text: I have been using jaggery to sweeten my tea in winters
Jaggery is being used by me to sweeten my tea in winters.
Jaggery is used by me to sweeten my tea in winters.
In winters jaggery was used by me to sweeten my tea.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is "**Jaggery is used by me to sweeten my tea in winters**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• In Active Voice, a sentence emphasizes the subject, performing an action.
 
• In Passive Voice, a sentence emphasizes the action or the object of the sentence.
 
• The given sentence is in the active voice and 'I' is the subject and 'jaggery' is the object.
 
• When we convert this sentence into passive voice, the subject 'I' of the active voice becomes the object 'me', the **object** '**jaggery**' **becomes** the **subject**.
 
• The passive format "is + V3" should be used.
 
• This is the active and passive voice rule for the present simple tense.
 
• Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question:
**Directions: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’**

Why did the teacher__ ask all four of you__ to stay back in class in the break?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"No improvement"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the given sentence, there is **no need to substitute the underlined segment**.
 
• The form of the verb '**ask**' is correct as '**did**' in the sentence is **an auxiliary verb** (or “helping verb”) that is **followed by the main verb**, which **carries the real verb meaning**.
 
• The **auxiliary verb 'did'** is marked **for past tense**, **but the main verb **is not. It appears **in its base form**.
 
• The **determiner 'all'**, the **number 'four'**, the **preposition 'of'** and the **pronoun 'you'** are **correctly used and placed** in the sentence.
 
• **Hence**, the correct answer is **option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **When there is an auxiliary verb**, the **main verb does not need to be marked for tense**, because the tense is shown in the auxiliary.
 
• However, in a **sentence** about the past **without an auxiliary verb**, the **main verb does need to be in the past tense form**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is a direct speech.
 
• The basic rules for changing or ____converting direct speech into indirect speech__:​
 __
 
• The commas and inverted commas are removed.
 
• The reporting verb 'said' is changed into 'told'.
 
• The **past simple** **tense** format 'Subject + V2 (made) + Object' in the direct speech will be changed into the **past perfect tense** format **'Subject + had + V3 (made) + Object' **in the indirect speech.
 
 
 
• From the following rules, we get the correct sentence as- option 2*.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The following table will enable us to know how tense changes into Indirect speech:

 
 

 Direct Speech
 Indirect Speech
 
 

 Present simple (Subject +V1st + Object)
 Past simple (Subject +V2 + Object)
 
 

 Present continuous (Subject +is/am/are+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Present perfect (Subject + has/have+V3+Object
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past simple (Subject+V2+Object)
 Past perfect (Subject+had+V3+Object)
 
 

 Past Continuous (Subject +was/were+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Past perfect continuous (Subject +had been+V1 +ing+ Object)
 
 

 Future simple (Subject+ will/shall+V1+object)
 Present Conditional (Subject+ would+V1+object)
 
 

 Future Continuous (Subject +will/shall+be+V1 +ing+ Object)
 Conditional Continuous (Subject +would+be+V1 +ing+ Object)
